title: Variables, Input, Output and One-Dimensional Arrays
intro: A short, independent catch-up: learn the essential knowledge, practise and review answers.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes a variable?
options: A value can be updated by assignment
It is always a fixed, permanent number
It stores every element of an array automatically
questions.answer: A value can be updated by assignment
questions.feedback: Assignment changes the value stored under a variable name.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the explanations, visual and model before answering.

blocks.title: Variables
blocks.text: A variable stores a value that can be updated using assignment. Use meaningful names.

blocks.title: Input and output
blocks.text: Input obtains information from a user or device; output displays or sends information.

blocks.title: Arrays
blocks.text: A one-dimensional array stores related values under one name, accessed using indexes.

blocks.title: Zero-based indexing
blocks.text: Index 0 is the first value; index 1 is the second, so the index differs from counting positions in everyday speech.

blocks.title: Visual model
blocks.caption: Use these linked concepts to explain your answer.

blocks.title: Worked example · Trace the array and variable assignments in a short quiz-mark program.
blocks.text: Create marks = [4, 7, 9]. The first value has index 0. Set total = marks[0] + marks[1], giving 11. Update marks[0] to 5. Recalculate total = marks[0] + marks[1] to obtain 12. Output total; explain why the value changed.

items: variable — Named storage for a value in a program.
assignment — Storing or updating a variable's value.
one-dimensional array — Indexed collection of values stored under one name.
index — Number specifying an array element's position.
